intake.lead: Files you upload in several batches are added to the existing list. Rows that were read become the evidence for an admin review request.

intake.addLead: Academic calendars, assessment schedules, blank report card or student record forms, and so on. Use synthetic or de-identified data.
intake.fileHint: You can add several files at once or in batches.
intake.readNote: CSV, TSV, TXT, XLSX (each sheet), and DOCX (tables in the document) are read. PDF tables are estimated from text positions, so check the evidence against the original. Scanned PDFs and other formats are stored and left waiting to be read.

intake.appendNote: New files are added to the existing list. Confirmed rules don't change when new files arrive; if the result differs, a new question is opened.
review.lead: Review what was estimated from the files, with its evidence, and confirm it. Each confirmation adds a new version; earlier versions and issued documents stay as they are.

common.name: Name
academics.lead: Set up school levels, school years, and terms. The term structure is saved as versions with a reason, and each school year's terms are created from a version.
academics.levelsEmpty: None yet. For example: elementary, middle, high, or your program names.
academics.ruleEmpty: None yet. Set it through file upload → admin review, or set it here with a reason.
academics.makeTerms: Create terms from term structure v{v}
academics.yearEnd: End (first day of the next school year)
academics.reasonPlaceholder: e.g., School academic policy, Article 3 (two-term year)
people.lead: Register students, staff, and guardians as people. Each student's enrollment record is kept as a date range per school level. Name changes are saved as new versions with a reason.
people.empty: No people to show. To register someone, use "Add person" below.
people.pick: Choose a person from the list to see their name history and enrollment here.
people.endConfirm: This ends the enrollment. An ended enrollment isn't reopened; you register a new one instead. Continue?
people.needLevel: To enroll a student, first create a school level in {link}.
people.renamed: Name saved as a new version.
courses.needYears: Create school years and terms in School setup first.
courses.needLevels: Create school levels in School setup first.
courses.lead: Set up subjects and course tracks, then offer courses for each term and school level with teachers and students. Track rules are saved as versions.
courses.col.subject: Subject
courses.noCandidates: No students are enrolled at this level as of the term start date.
courses.addWhen: Students can be added while a course is open for sign-up or in progress (planned courses: after the term starts).
courses.labelSaved: Listing saved as a new version.
courses.labelNote: Listings are saved as versions per use. If someone else changed the same use in the meantime, saving is refused; reload and save again.
courses.noTypes: No tracks. For example: required, elective, student-proposed.
courses.ruleSaved: Track rule saved as a new version.
courses.publishable: Can be shown on the website
grades.lead: Set assessments, enter scores and comments, then close the course. Results and comments are never overwritten; each change is a new entry. A closing version freezes the values with the policy and scale used.
grades.pickCourse: Choose a course on the Courses page, then open ‘Enter and close grades’.
grades.onlyTeachers: · Only this course's teachers or a school admin can enter grades.
grades.noAssessments: No assessments. For example: midterm 30 · final 40 · performance 30 (weights are relative).
grades.archiveConfirm: Archive this assessment? Entered results stay, but it's left out of the closing calculation.
grades.narrativesSub: Detailed abilities and notes / course comment
grades.narrativeSaved: Comment saved as a new entry.
grades.notClosed: Not closed yet. Closing calculates raw, final, grade, and completion from current scores and freezes them as a version.
grades.confirmCorrection: Create a new closing version? The previous version stays as it is.
grades.confirmClose: Close this course? After closing, an admin corrects scores with a reason.
grades.noScales: No scales. Add a preset scale below.
grades.noPolicy: No version — raw scores use 2 decimals, final scores are whole numbers, and population SD is used.
grades.policySaved: Grading policy saved as a new version.
grid.noAssessments: There are no assessments (course-level) to enter scores for.
grid.correctionReason: Reason for correction (closed course: school admins only)
attendance.lead: Daily attendance is saved as entries; a correction is a new entry pointing to the earlier one. Attendance types and reasons are school codes, and summaries use enrolled instructional days as the denominator.
attendance.notOnCalendar: This day isn't on the instructional calendar. Attendance can still be taken, but summaries only count days marked as instructional on the calendar.
attendance.noStudents: No students enrolled on this day.
attendance.endAfterStart: The end date must be after the start date.
attendance.thresholds: Chronic absenteeism: days absent ≥ {chronic}% of enrolled days · attendance minimum: present ≥ {min}% (grading policy version policy.attendance)
attendance.noDays: No days set for this month.
attendance.noYear: No school year includes this date. Create one in {link} first.
register.noStudents: No students are enrolled at this level on this day.
docs.lead: Issue documents from the confirmed term rule and the current template. Issued documents keep the values as they were at the time.
docs.confirmFirst: Confirm the term rule in Admin review first.
docs.previewBasis: Based on current rule and template
docs.previewEmpty: A preview appears once a rule is confirmed.
docs.field.title: Document title
docs.templateSaved: Template v{v} saved. Earlier issued documents don't change.

pkg.adminOnly: School admins turn packages on and off.

nav.placements.title: Isolation tiers
placement.title: Isolation tiers
placement.lead: Decide where each school runs: shared, extended, dedicated or independent. Every change is kept as a new version; the actual move (new database and deployment) follows docs/SCHOOL-MOVE.md separately. Costs are estimated ranges, not prices.
placement.tier.shared.desc: Shared database and app. Most schools
placement.tier.extended.desc: Shared core + a school-only annex (own features, integrations)
placement.tier.dedicated.desc: Core records in a school-only database and deployment (run by us)
placement.tier.independent.desc: Installed on the school's or organization's own account or server (run by the school)
placement.movedBanner: This school has moved to a new address: {url}
placement.movedTitle: Your school has moved to a new address
admin.lead: Create schools and manage licenses, status, prices, and billing. Entering a school shows its screens as they are, and each entry is logged for that school.
admin.billsNote: Records of finalized expected amounts. Payment integration comes separately once a payment provider is chosen.
adminc.suspendBody: Members will no longer be able to use this school's screens. Records aren't deleted, and changing the status back lets them continue.
adminc.statusBody: The status change is logged for the school.
adminc.billBody: Creates the {period} billing record for {name}. No payment is made, but {strong}
adminc.billStrong: a finalized record can't be edited or deleted.
adminc.repoLinked: The GitHub repository was linked too.
adminc.created: Created {name} and invited {email} as school admin.{extra}
adminc.priceSaved: Price saved. Each school's amount uses the new price at its next license change.
adminc.priceNote: Saved license versions keep the price from that time (price history is preserved).
usage.lead: Estimates the monthly cost from each school's file storage, AI use, and external agent actions. Amounts are USD estimates, not a bill (prices checked {checked}; R2 storage ${r2}/GB, DB disk ${db}/GB). Visitor downloads from R2 are free and aren't counted.
usage.kpi.toMove: {n, plural, one {# file to move to R2} other {# files to move to R2}}
usage.notConfigured: Not configured · storing in the database
usage.r2On: New website images and PDFs are stored in R2 (private bucket), and visitors get a 10-minute signed link after the visibility check. Copy existing files with the button below (the database copy stays).
usage.r2Off: Set the Vercel environment variables R2_ACCOUNT_ID · R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID · R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY · R2_BUCKET and redeploy to turn it on. Guide: docs/SETUP-R2.md
usage.bySchoolSub: Last 30 days · per-school amounts are before the included allowance
usage.aiNote: AI is the sum of estimated costs recorded when in-app AI features run (0 for now, since there are none yet). External agents (the school's Claude or Codex subscription) aren't platform charges; only their actions are counted.
usage.copy: Copy database files to R2 (25 at a time, {n} left)
base.lead: Releasing a new baseline version (code lists, scales, grading policy) sends a proposal to each school. School status is collected only through report-contract snapshots.
base.contract: Contract {contract}. To change it, create a new version and publish both for a while.
base.title: Control baseline
base.published: New baseline released. A proposal goes to each school.
base.publishConfirm: Release a new baseline? Every school gets an update proposal (applied only when the school accepts).
cc.lead: Decision requests from sessions and your instructions, in one place. Pick an option or add instructions; the control session passes them to the session or starts a new one. Sessions don't stop to wait for answers (reversible work proceeds with the recommended option first). For the to-do list, see {link}.
cc.kpi.answeredHint: Instructions for control to send to sessions
cc.title: Title
cc.detailHint: Background, scope, and done criteria. The session starts from this text alone.
cc.extraHint: Conditions to add to the option, or new work. Sent to the session as written.
integ.lead: Link each school's own GitHub repository, Claude Code sessions, Codex environment, and Vercel or Supabase projects, and generate the prompt for opening a work session for that school. Only addresses and descriptions are stored, never tokens or keys.
integ.noSchoolsBody: Create a school in Schools & licenses first.
integ.col.label: Name · address
integ.openSession: Open a work session for this school
integ.openNote: Paste this when opening a new task in Claude Code (claude.ai/code) or Codex. After opening the session, add its address on the left as a ‘Claude Code session’ or ‘Codex environment’ to track it per school.
integ.tokensNote: Work tokens issued by school admins. Flags tokens expiring within 30 days and no-expiry tokens unused for over 180 days. Each school admin extends or revokes them in /site settings.
integ.col.name: Name
insp.title: Claude inspection access
insp.lead: The control Claude session works as platform admin without signing in (ADR 0024). School entries and changes are logged just like a human platform admin's. Tokens are issued and revoked only on this page.
insp.onceBody: Paste it into the {credential} the Claude session opens (host onschools.vercel.app, header x-inspector-token). Don't paste it into the chat.
insp.note: The token itself isn't stored, only its hash. Issuing and revoking are logged; revoke right away if anything looks wrong.
lab.lead: See plans, tools, methods, research, and to-dos as cards. Open a card to see tables and diagrams; write an ‘Instruction’ at the bottom and a session continues from it and reports back in place.
lab.banner: Work waiting on your decision is in the {link}{open}. Lab card instructions also go to sessions through the control center.
lab.threadNote: Your instructions for this item. They go to a session through the control center; the session updates this item's content (tables, diagrams) or does the work, then reports below. Review the result, then close it as ‘Done’ or write the next instruction.
lab.title: Title
lab.help: Format help (tables, metrics, flows, bars, steps)
lab.sent: Instruction sent. It goes to a session through the control center.
lab.directivePlaceholder: e.g., Add a 30-school case to the cost table and lay out the extended-tier pilot steps as a flow.
design.title: Design archetypes
design.lead: The same school scene (synthetic data) drawn in eight screen structures. Beyond color, the navigation, layout grid, type and size, density, and key interaction all differ. Click a thumbnail to open it full screen and use the bar below to move between archetypes.
design.banner: Real products usually mix rather than pick one. Choose one {shell} and a few {types}. For example: shell from #1 academic workspace, question review from #8 inbox, course and roster tables from #7 grid, platform overview from #4 analytics. Click ‘Choose this direction’ on each archetype you like to log it on the Lab board.
design.axesNote: Seven axes side by side for each archetype. Scroll sideways if the table is wide.
design.note: Only structural principles were borrowed; no logos, assets, or distinctive screens from reference products. Research notes and sources are in docs/research/dashboard-rea-2026-11.md.

site.token.connect.risk: The token stays in the AI chat history. Choose only the types, addresses and permissions you need, and keep the expiry short (7 days). When the work is done, revoke it to stop it at once; what it did stays in the list below.
site.token.connect.showToken: Show token only (to put in the SCHOOL_AGENT_TOKEN environment variable)
site.token.title: AI workspace
site.token.lead: Hand website work to an AI you use, such as Codex or Claude Code. Choose the scope and permissions and issue a token to get the {b}. Just paste that text into your AI chat. No token can touch settings, members or other schools, and publishing works only when you grant the publish permission.
site.token.nameHint: Make it easy to tell what you're handing over
site.token.longWarning: If a long-lived or no-expiry token leaks, it can be used until you revoke it. Choose only the permissions you need, and check 'Last used' in the list now and then.
site.token.shortHint: Shorter is safer. You can extend it before it ends.
site.token.keys: Items to assign (none selected = all of the chosen types)
site.token.keysEmpty: The chosen types have no items yet.
site.token.autoNote: {b}: visitors see it as soon as the agent creates an item or saves a new version (no draft step). The publish permission turns on too. We recommend fixing the addresses and keeping the expiry short. If something is published by mistake, roll back to a previous version or unpublish it here.
site.token.autoOneSession: Use it in one session only.
site.token.autoOneSessionBody: If several sessions share it, one session's work in progress can go public as is.
site.token.publishNote: With the 'Publish' permission, when you tell the agent to publish, visitors see it right away without you clicking here. Creating or editing alone never publishes. It's recorded in the publish and activity logs, and you can unpublish here at any time.
site.token.sessionGuideTitle: Issue a separate token per session.
site.token.sessionGuide: If several AI chats (sessions) share one token, it's hard to tell who did what, and revoking it stops them all at once. Put an operator and session name in the connection text and they show under 'Activity' below (reported by the AI, not a verified identity).
site.token.extendDaysHint: Used by the 'Extend' buttons in the list. Extends from the current end date (the token value stays the same).
site.token.sharedAuto: ⚠ Auto-publish token used by several sessions
site.token.shared: ⚠ Shared by several sessions — issue one per session

site.import.lead: Choose an export bundle (zip) made from the old site to turn its pages, news, stories and supporter pages into {b}. For items that already exist, it checks whether someone edited them — if not, it replaces them with a new version; if so, it only fills empty fields (adding a new version without erasing history). Publishing and opening the website are done separately after you check the drafts.

site.tpl.description: Each template comes with a design (colors, fonts, home screen) and a set of pages. Preview the finished look, then choose one to create draft pages. You publish them yourself after filling in the content.
site.tpl.pageCount: {n, plural, one {# page now} other {# pages now}}
site.tpl.slots: {n, plural, one {# field to fill} other {# fields to fill}}
site.tpl.research: Research basis: websites of Korean public and alternative schools, US private schools, international schools, Christian schools, NSW (Australia) public schools, and Thai public schools (repository docs/research/homepage-templates-2026-11.md).
site.tpl.design.noSite: You can choose the ‘{name}’ look in settings after setting up the website (its address).
site.tpl.design.toggle: Also switch the look to the ‘{name}’ design
site.tpl.design.openNote: The website is open, so switching changes what visitors see (colors, fonts) right away. Current look: {current}. You can change it back in settings at any time.
site.tpl.design.closedNote: Current look: {current}. You can change it in settings at any time.
site.tpl.apply.done: {n, plural, one {Created # draft page} other {Created # draft pages}}{skipped}{design}. Fill in the content before publishing.
site.tpl.apply.existing: Existing pages ({pages}) stay untouched; only the other pages are created.
site.tpl.autofill.title: Fill from school files
site.tpl.autofill.intro: Upload a school profile or handout (PDF, DOCX, TXT) and we'll suggest matching text for each field (a first pass based on keyword rules). Only what you confirm goes into a new draft version, and fields the school already wrote are left alone. Photo fields are chosen from images uploaded to the website.
site.tpl.autofill.done: {n, plural, one {Filled # field} other {Filled # fields}} and created a new draft version{kept}. Check it in the page list before publishing.
site.tpl.autofill.kept: ({n, plural, one {# field} other {# fields}} the school already wrote kept as is)
site.tpl.autofill.missingPages: Fields on pages that don't exist yet ({pages}) can't be filled. Start with the template first.
site.tpl.autofill.noMatch: No matching text found. Fill in the fields yourself or hand it to the school AI.
site.tpl.autofill.agent: Hand off to the school AI
site.tpl.autofill.agentHelp: In Website → Settings → AI workspace, issue a token of type ‘page’ (read and edit), paste the connection text into the school AI, and ask it to “fill the template's empty fields from school files.” The school AI reads the field guide from GET /api/agent/templates and saves new draft versions of the pages.
site.tpl.migrate.title: Move from existing website
site.tpl.migrate.intro: Enter your current school website address and we'll read up to 8 pages on that site and suggest content for each field. Only public pages are read, following the site's robots.txt. Only what you confirm goes into a new draft version, and only the images you pick are imported.
site.tpl.migrate.pagesRead: {n, plural, one {# page read} other {# pages read}}: {pages}{skipped}
site.tpl.migrate.pickImages: Choose from {n, plural, one {# image} other {# images}} on the old site
site.tpl.migrate.consent: Only import photos showing students if the student and guardian have given permission to publish them.
site.tpl.migrate.imagesDone: {n, plural, one {Imported # image} other {Imported # images}} to the website{failed}.
site.tpl.migrate.done: {n, plural, one {Filled # field} other {Filled # fields}} from the old site and created a new draft version. Check it in the page list before publishing.
site.tpl.start.title: Move your existing website to a new design
site.tpl.start.intro: Enter your current website address and we'll read up to 8 public pages on that site (following robots.txt) and recommend a template that fits the content. You can try other templates, and only the content you confirm moves into drafts in the new design. You publish it yourself.
site.tpl.start.urlHint: Address of your school website's home page, starting with https://
site.tpl.start.fillable: {n, plural, one {# field can be filled} other {# fields can be filled}}
site.tpl.start.noMatch: No content found for this template's fields. You can start with just the template and hand the rest to the school AI.
site.tpl.start.remaining: Fields not moved: {labels} — write them yourself after moving, or hand them to the school AI.
site.tpl.start.images: After moving, pick from the old site's {n, plural, one {# image} other {# images}} in ‘Move from existing website’ below the ‘{name}’ preview.
site.tpl.start.done: Created {pages, plural, one {# draft page} other {# draft pages}} in the ‘{name}’ design and filled {n, plural, one {# field} other {# fields}} from the old site{skipped}{design}. Nothing is published yet.
site.tpl.start.notMoved: Found on the old site but not moved — check needed
site.tpl.agent.summary: Text to hand off to the school AI (Codex, Claude Code)
site.tpl.agent.help: Filling missing fields and creating images for photo fields is done with the school's own AI subscription (no platform cost). Paste the text below into the AI chat together with a work token issued in ‘AI workspace’. The token is not included in this text.
site.tpl.agent.label: Text for the school AI
site.tpl.agent.intro: We are moving our school website to the '{name}' template (new design). Old site: {start}
site.tpl.agent.token: Work only with the work token the school admin issued in 'AI workspace' (type page, permissions read, upload, edit), and do not publish (a person publishes after review).
site.tpl.agent.docs: Guide: repository docs docs/agents/site-migrate.md and docs/agents/README.md (API).
site.tpl.agent.fill: 1. Find the still-empty fields on the old site ({n} pages read), fill them, and save a new version: {slots}
site.tpl.agent.check: 1. Compare the filled fields with the old site, fix any errors, and save a new version
site.tpl.agent.images: 2. Photo fields: {slots} — use photos from the old site that the school has rights to, or create illustrations without real people's faces, upload them with POST /api/agent/assets, and add them to a new version of that page
site.tpl.agent.report: {step}. Report to a person the remaining [ ] placeholders and facts that need checking (tuition, dates, contacts)
site.tpl.detail.title: Template: {name}
site.tpl.detail.sampleNote: Shown filled with the made-up school '{school}'. When you start, [ ] placeholders go in instead of the sample text.
site.tpl.detail.guideNote: This is what goes into the school's pages when you start. Replace the [ ] placeholders with your school's content.
site.tpl.detail.slots: Fields to fill on this page
site.tpl.detail.adminOnly: Templates are applied by a school admin.
site.tpl.view.label: Preview content
site.tpl.live.label: Template preview
site.tpl.live.sampleNote: An example from the made-up school ‘{school}’.
